articles.title: Interest rates continue to rise
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
Government borrowing rates continue to rise, both on short and long maturities. As usual, the US is leading the way and we believe that short-term expectations of the Fed are the main driver for the longer maturities as well. Yesterday, the US 10-year yield even passed 5%, a level that is often highlighted as psychologically important for the market. Government borrowing rates in Europe are following suit, and the interest rate differential between safe Germany and more vulnerable issuers such as France and Italy continued to rise. The rise in interest rates is directly linked to the deteriorating situation in energy prices, a trend that only looks set to continue (more below). The stock market turned lower yesterday, first in Europe and then also in the US. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq fell 0.5% and 0.6%, respectively. Rising rates play its role, but the discussion in recent days about slowing down AI development also dragged down technology companies. The stock market in Asia is mostly down slightly, although Japan's Nikkei seems to be moving in the opposite direction. Stock market futures indicate a small rise in Europe, but continued declines in the US.
It's not a super heavy day from a statistical perspective, but there is clearly still a little for most people who are interested in the UK, the euro area and the US. Today and tomorrow, an investor conference will be held in Toronto, a step to try to break Canada's economic dependence on the US. Mark Carney also yesterday aired thoughts about finding a "unique alliance" with the EU ahead of next week's visit to Brussels. 
Really the wrong direction for energy. 
Oil prices are rising after the Houthis' attack on Saudi Arabia's east-west pipeline, which has so far been the key to partially maintaining oil supply from the region. Brent oil is now trading around USD 107/barrel and European gas prices are above EUR 80/MWh (just over 60 a month ago). Although it is currently being replenished a little faster than normal, the low gas inventories in Europe are an important part of the risk picture ahead of the winter. The rising price of gas has contributed to pushing up electricity prices in Europe and also here in the Nordic region, but yesterday's price peak can unfortunately be viewed as a foretaste. The unusually low levels in the water reservoirs in Norway reinforce the picture that a prolonged period of windless cold can be costly in a couple of months. The only slightly positive part that is currently visible is that a super-El Niño sometimes means a warmer winter in Europe, something that could be dampening. But even that can have a negative effect, especially for us in the Nordic countries, as the weather phenomenon sometimes causes high pressure with severe cold to get stuck in the region during the second half of winter.
Nordic key stories
Continued focus on the election.
 In Sweden, the parties are waiting for tomorrow's final count, which in any case can helpfully set the starting point for the more in-depth talks, even if there is already a "buzz" about possible openings. As expected, the election results offered marginal market reactions. Our thoughts about the election outcome you find 
here
. According to the latest figures, there is still 176-173 in the distribution of seats between the opposition and the Tidö parties. According to election forecasters, the "last" seat weighs between the Left Party and the Moderates.

articles.title: Fortsatt stigande räntor
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Statslåneräntor fortsätter upp, både på korta och långa löptider. I vanlig ordning är USA ledande och vi bedömer att det är kortsiktiga förväntningar på Fed som är den huvudsakliga drivkraften även på de längre löptiderna. Igår passerade den amerikanska 10-årsräntan till och med 5%, en nivå som ofta lyfts fram som psykologiskt viktig för marknaden. Statslåneräntor i Europa följer med upp, och ränteskillnaden mellan trygga Tyskland i förhållande till mer utsatta emittenter som Frankrike och Italien fortsatte stiga. Ränteuppgången är direkt kopplad till det försämrade läget för energipriserna, en utveckling som bara ser ut att fortsätta (mer nedan). Börsen vände ned igår, först i Europa och sen även i USA. S&P 500 och Nasdaq backade 0,5% respektive 0,6%. Ränteuppgången spelar viss roll, men de senaste dagarnas diskussion om att bromsa AI-utvecklingen drog också ner teknikbolagen. Aktiemarknaden i Asien går mestadels ner något, även om japanska Nikkei verkar gå i motsatt riktning. Börsterminer indikerar uppgång i Europa, men fortsatt nedgång USA.
Det är ingen supertung dag utifrån ett statistikperspektiv, men det finns helt klart ändå lite för de flesta som är intresserade av Storbritannien, euroområdet och USA. Idag och imorgon hålls en investerarkonferens i Toronto, ett steg att försöka bryta Kanadas ekonomiska beroende av USA. Mark Carney ventilerade även igår tankar om att hitta en ”unik allians” med EU inför nästa veckas besök i Bryssel. 
Verkligen fel riktning på energin. 
Oljepriset stiger efter Huthiernas attack på Saudiarabiens öst-västliga pipeline, som hittills utgjort nyckeln till att delvis upprätthålla oljeutbudet från regionen. Brentoljan handlas nu kring 107 USD/fat och europeiska gaspriser ligger över 80 EUR/MWh (drygt 60 för en månad sedan). Även om det just nu fylls på lite snabbare än normalt utgör de låga gaslagren i Europa en viktig del i riskbilden inför vintern. Det stigande gaspriset har bidragit till att trycka upp elpriserna i Europa och även här i Norden, men gårdagens pristopp var nog dessvärre bara en försmak. De ovanligt låga nivåerna i vattenmagasinen i Norge förstärker bilden av att en längre period av vindstilla kyla kan bli kostsamt om ett par månader. Den enda lite positiva delen som just nu syns är att en super-El Niño ibland innebär en varmare vinter i Europa, något som skulle kunna vara dämpande. Men även det kan ha en negativ effekt, framför allt för oss i Norden, då väderfenomenet ibland gör att högtryck med rejäl kyla fastnar i regionen under andra halvan av vintern.
Sverige
Fortsatt valfokus.
 I Sverige väntar partierna på morgondagens sluträkning, som i alla fall hjälpligt kan sätta startpunkten för de mer ingående samtalen, även om det redan nu ”surras” om eventuella öppningar. Som väntat erbjöd valresultatet marginella marknadsreaktioner. Övriga funderingar om valutgången, samarbetspusslet och tidsschema för budget hittar du skriftligt 
här
, alternativt gårdagens eftervalsanalys från oss 
här
, eller poddversion 
här
. Enligt de senaste siffrorna står det fortfarande 176-173 i mandatfördelningen mellan oppositionen och Tidöpartierna. Enligt valprognosörer väger det ”sista” mandatet mellan Vänsterpartiet och Moderaterna.
Svenska kronan försvagades ytterligare igår, och en EUR/SEK-kurs strax under 11,30 kan jämföras med läget förra sommaren. Både bensin och diesel fortsätter upp och bensinpriset (ca 18 kr/l) ligger nu över nivån strax innan den stora, tillfälliga, skattesänkningen infördes. Dieselpriset (ca 23 kr/l) ligger samtidigt i paritet med priserna i slutet av april. Gårdagens 3-kronersnotering för el i elområdet 4 har halverats inför idag.

articles.title: We revise our forecast and expect a September hike after August CPI
articles.heading: Fed Preview
articles.fulltext:
August CPI surprised on the upside for a 0.3% m/m increase, raising some question marks about the degree of improvement in the underlying inflation trend. Given the strong emphasis within the Fed on the monthly data, we shift our forecast and now expect a 25 bp hike in September. Upward pressure on the oil price after renewed escalations in the conflict in the Middle East is an upside risk going forward. The market prices nearly 90% for a September hike and we think an unchanged rate would be badly received by bond markets. 
Key points
Policy rate expected to be raised by 25 bp to 3.75-4.00%.
CPI disappointment points to another too high core PCE but the upcoming revision is an uncertain factor
Market prices 90% (22 bp) for a September hike
Bloomberg consensus predicts unchanged rates, but analysts are evenly split
New forecasts but Warsh will not use them as a signaling tool
Inflation trends need to improve by year-end for the Fed stop at one hike 
Rate hike in September is now the main scenario
Market pricing for a September hike moved from almost 70 to nearly 90% after the August CPI data. The y/y rate for core CPI declined further, from 2.5% to 2.4%, but the monthly increase came in above expectations at 0.3%, though on the lower side (0.29%). The details were not all bad; volatile components, including tourist services, contributed to the faster price increases while goods prices were marginally lower than expected (read more about the August CPI 
here
). Our estimate for the Fed’s key measure core PCE points to another 0.3% m/m increase, though the upcoming revision of this data on 30 September is an uncertain factor. Methodological changes are expected to lower the PCE by at least a couple of tenths of percentage points, which will still leave the core PCE at an elevated around 3.0% y/y rate. 
This puts the Fed under pressure to deliver a hike in September to bolster its inflation credibility. We are now changing our forecast for the 15-16 September meeting to a 25 bp hike to a range of 3.75-4.00%. Higher energy prices, back above USD 100/bl, is an upside risk going forward. Waiting until the next meeting on 27-28 October could put the Fed in a difficult situation, given the proximity to the midterm elections on November 3. Analysts in Bloomberg's consensus survey are divided, but nearly 50 percent expect a hike on Wednesday. Also, a relatively large portion of the responses in the survey were provided before the August CPI. Most of the responses provided after the data forecast a hike. 
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has been very clear that it is the responsibility of the Fed to make sure that inflation returns to target. He has been equally clear that the Fed should not signal its next step. This means that the Fed should now be data dependent and take its decisions on a meeting-by-meeting basis. Inflation data during the fall will be key for whether the Fed can stop at one hike to safeguard credibility. We continue to see scope for renewed disinflation once the temporary effects from tariffs, energy and, to some extent, AI on IT, pass. Whether the Fed will get enough evidence on this in the coming months is uncertain, however. For now, we expect the Fed to stop at one credibility-strengthening rate hike in September and that the next step will be a rate cut in fall 2027, followed by another cut in early 2028. However, if underlying inflation trends have not improved by the December meeting, and the economy remains resilient, the Fed may have no choice but to deliver another, and final, rate hike in December. Continued upward pressure on yields will work in the other direction, with markets now doing some of the job for the Fed. Markets are already pricing a succession of rate hikes until mid-year 2026 and the Fed must now hope that delivering a hike could calm market doubts of the Fed’s willingness to do what it takes.
The Fed is split but tolerance for inflation above target is running low 
Three regional Fed presidents – Beth Hammack, Lorie Logan and Neel Kashkari – voted for a hike at the July meeting. At the same time, several members of the Governing Board – Lisa Cook, John Williams, Michael Barr and Christopher Waller – have signaled that they could consider leaving the policy rate on hold in September if data supports continued progress for inflation. We believe the August CPI did not pass the test even for Fed doves to avoid a September hike, but equally not being bad enough to make them commit to a series of rate hikes. Kevin Warsh’s hawkish speech at Jackson Hole succeeded in convincing the market that he is serious about inflation and that he sees changes in the Fed’s policy rate as the main tool to achieve the target. We do not think that Warsh wanted to send a signal for the September meeting given his opposition to forward guidance, but his policy conclusion was similar to that of the other members: The Fed must be confident that underlying inflation is moving to the target and if not, the Fed will need to act.
A decision to hike needs to have large support
If the Fed, in line with our and the market expectations, decides to tighten policy we think that the Committee will strive to build a consensus, given the risks for intensifying political pressures from the White House and the fact that members seem to share the view that inflation cannot be allowed to diverge so much from target for so long. 
Warsh to repeat his message from Jackson Hole
We expect Warsh to continue to stress his commitment to bringing inflation back to target at the post-meeting press conference. Warsh’s earlier press conferences have been criticized for not including a clearer explanation of the Fed’s policy decisions and the reaction function. We believe that Warsh will stick to his view that the Fed should not guide the markets on their next step but the Chair will still need to explain the rational for a rate hike and answer questions on whether or not this will need to be followed by more steps and provide some insights into the Fed’s reaction function. 
New projections without input from Warsh
In September FOMC members are, as usual, expected to deliver new forecasts for the economy and rates. Warsh has been clear that he thinks the Fed should stop releasing its own forecasts and he has chosen not to provide his own. However, we do not expect any changes to communication policy until next year, when we see it as likely that the Fed either abolishes the projections or chooses to release them together with the publication of minutes, to downplay their role as a signaling tool. 
No significant changes to the economic outlook
We do not see a need for the Fed to make other than minor changes to the economic projections compared to June and expect them to continue to project healthy, slightly above trend, growth, a slight decline in the unemployment rate towards the longer-run and above target inflation in 2026 and 2027 before returning to target by end 2028. Members usually add one more year in September and we expect these projections to be close to the current longer-run projections.

Members are likely to project one 2026 rate hike including the September hike 
We expect the median rate to continue to project one hike by December followed by rate cuts in 2027 and 2028. The urgency in getting inflation back to target could, however, argue for postponing rate cuts until later in the period or in 2028 and 2029, rather than 2027 and 2028. If we are right in our expectations, the Fed will still send a dovish signal compared to current market pricing of nearly two full hikes by year-end and another one to two rate hikes in 2027 (accumulated around 90 bps by September 2027). However, we expect Chair Warsh to downplay any signals from the forecasts and, like last time, we do not expect him to participate with his own projections.

articles.title: A new 20y bond to be launched
articles.heading: NGB Spotlight
articles.fulltext:
Norges Bank will introduce a new 20y bond via syndication. The deal was announced today and is expected to be concluded tomorrow. Due to the inversion in the long end of the swap curve the new 20y bond will likely have a negative yield pick-up vs. NST485 (2042). Still, the market will demand some new issue premium in ASW terms, and the indicative price target is likely to include a discount, with possibility of tightening during the book building. We see an IPT in the MS +6 to +8bps area as reasonable.
Details on the new issue
Norges Bank announced in its 
borrowing and strategy report for 2026
 that it aimed to issue a new 20y bond in September or October via syndication. The mandate requires maturities up to 10 years, but Norges Bank issued a 20y bond in 2022 and a 15y bond in 2024. The bank argues that introducing a new 20y bond will reduce the annual refinancing requirement, facilitate the participation of a wider range of investor groups (primarily domestic) and reduce supply pressure in maturities of up to 10 years.
The deal was just announced, and primary dealer banks (SEB, Danske Bank, Deutsche Bank, DNB Carnegie and Nordea) will act as joint bookrunners. With Norges Bank’s upcoming rate decision (Sep 24) and autumn school holiday in Norway (week 40/41), the timing of the announcement was not surprising. The bank has guided towards NOK 5-10bn in volume. We expect demand to be sufficient for Norges Bank to issue the maximum amount, which has been the case in earlier syndications.
The following details on the new bond (NST491) have been announced:
Maturity date:
 24 September 2046 (20.3y).
Coupon:
 Not yet announced (our best guess is 4.50% or 4.625%).  
Issue size:
 Not yet announced, but in its borrowing and strategy report the bank has guided at NOK 5-10bn excl. government’s own holdings. 
Timing:
 The deal was announced today, and “the transaction will be launched in the near future”. We expect it to be launched later today with the deal being tomorrow’s business. 
Indicative Price Target:
 Not yet announced. We expect a first guidance in the MS +6 to +8bps area (mid/mid).
Fair pricing and outlook
In Germany and Sweden, the 15s20s swap curves are trading near flat, while the yield curves have a positive slope. In Norway, however, the long end of the swap curve is inverted with the 15s20s curve trading around -10bps. NST488 (05/2039) trades with a positive yield pick-up vs. NST490 (06-2036) of 
~3.5bps
, while the yield spread between NST485 (10/2042) and NST488 trades around 
-3.5bps
. The inversion of the swap curve implies that the new 20y bond will likely have a negative yield pick-up vs. NST485 (2042). Still, the market will demand some new issue premium in ASW terms, and we believe a fair level to be around 
MS +3 to +5bps
 (mid/mid) implying an approx. yield level around 
4.48-4.50%
 and maturity-matched spread vs. Germany around 61bps. The indicative price target is likely to include a discount, with possibility for a tightening during the book building as has been the norm in previous syndications. We thus see an indicative price target around MS 
+6 to +8bps (mid/mid) as reasonable.
Looking at the historical trading pattern, the long end has outperformed on a spread basis vs. swaps following the introduction of a new bond. Elevated inflation and the potential for another rate hike could weigh on bonds, however, inflation prospects have improved recently with rate spreads vs. EUR and SEK having tightened markedly recently. This has also been reflected in yield spreads vs. Germany. We regard current market pricing, implying a 55% chance for a September hike and a policy rate peak of 4.60%, as fair. Moreover, the supply outlook is supportive. Assuming NOK 10bn in the syndication, Norges Bank will have issued a total of NOK 91bn YTD implying only NOK 9-19bn in regular tap auctions for the remainder of the year. Due to the syndication, Norges Bank has cancelled the plan tap auction and buyback auction scheduled for Wednesday.

articles.title: Tricky government negotiations await
articles.heading: Sweden general election 2026
articles.fulltext:
Key points
Marginal majority for opposition according to preliminary results.
Tricky government negotiations are expected.
Small market reactions – government finances are strong, institutions are strong and growth is improving.
The Swedish election outcome is still not final, with the last votes counted on Wednesday. The current standing gives the centre-left opposition 176 (of 349) mandates and the current right-wing coalition (Tidö) coalition 173 mandates. Votes from Swedes living abroad, which are still to be counted, could lean in favour of the Tidö-coalition favour but it looks unlikely to be enough to secure 176 mandates.
Fragmented parliamentary landscape
This sets the scene for a very complicated government formation. The opposition parties (Social Democrats, Left, Greens and Centre Party) may agree on climate-related and somewhat more liberal immigration policies but disagree on topics such as taxation and corporate policies. More specifically, the Centre Party (C) has said it refuses to support a government including the Left Party (V), while V says it won’t support a Social Democratic led government unless they are part of it. In short: unless V or C crosses one of their red lines, the opposition cannot gather sufficient support to form majority.
Can C join the Tidö side? They would then have to cross another red line, as they refuse to support a government relying on support from the anti-immigration Sweden Democrats. Instead, C advocates a ’grand coalition’ in the middle, excluding both the Left Party and the Sweden Democrats. For this to happen, C must convince at least the Liberals and the Christian Democrats to change side; difficult, to say the least. And even if they manage, agreeing on a budget seems even more difficult.
In any event, government formation is likely to take time, as was the case in both preceding elections. After the election in 2018, a new red-green government took office on January 21, 2019 – 129 days after election day.
Small market reactions
As expected, market reactions have been muted and are likely to remain contained, even if the government formation and budget process takes time, consistent with previous episodes of a hung government. Sweden’s public finances are favourable, with low government debt both in an international and a historical perspective, and the institutional framework is strong.
Furthermore, the fragmented parliamentary landscape suggest it may be difficult for any party to gain support for the more controversial political proposals, including a bank tax and wealth tax. The Centre party is strongly opposed most suggestions of higher taxation policies apart from some energy taxes. More specifically, energy taxation might be one of few areas where the opposition parties agree, with higher energy taxes as a result.
Budget process likely to take time
There is no formal deadline for forming a new government, meaning that, in theory, a caretaker government could remain in office until the next general election – although this is highly unlikely. If no new government has been formed by 12 November, the current government remains in office as a caretaker government and submits the Budget Bill. There are no formal laws restricting the contents of such a budget, but constitutional praxis suggest that a caretaker’s budget proposal should avoid politically controversial and clearly partisan measures. Focus should be on current and urgent measures.
The Riksdag decides on a budget. A budget is adopted if a majority in the Riksdag votes in favour, or at least not against, the proposal. Opposition parties/coalitions may also present their own budget proposals. This means that the caretaker government may need to govern on an opposition budget, which was the case in 2019. Then, the S-led caretaker government presented a stripped down, neutral budget, but the opposition parties’ joint alternative budget won support in the Riksdag – subsequently becoming the government budget for 2019.
A scenario in which a Social Democratic government rules on a right-wing budget is possible. The preliminary outcome of the election suggest voters favour more liberal, right-leaning economic policy, even if the centre-left opposition gains a majority of mandates.
What happens if parties cannot agree on a budget?
The Swedish government does not shut down if a budget hasn’t been agreed upon by January 2027. Instead, appropriations in the latest accepted budget runs on. The Riksdag can also decide on single temporary changes to revenues/appropriations. The current budget includes many temporary measures, aimed mostly at households. In case no new budget can be agreed upon, these will lapse as previously decided.
A new government can make amendments to the caretaker budget after it has taken office, primarily through the Spring Bill Proposal. However, additional amending budgets can be submitted under special circumstances. The Riksdag may also make changes to revenues and/or appropriations if the initiative to such a proposal has been raised by the Riksdag itself (and not the government).
During pandemic and the energy crisis (also following the war in Iran) a string of budget amendments was presented and passed. In practise, the government thus has large scope to change the budget during the year if it has support from a majority in parliament.

articles.title: Difficult government negotiations await after close election
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
Despite higher interest rates, the S&P 500 rose by nearly one percent on Friday 
and is more than 10 percent higher than before the Iran war, although the index has fallen slightly from its mid-August highs. Stock market futures, on the other hand, are pointing lower this morning, driven by higher oil prices after Saudi Arabia shut down an oil pipeline as a result of attacks. A meeting between Iran and other Gulf states on how to open the Strait of Hormuz ended without results due to disagreement. Brent crude rises by about three dollars to 108 USD/barrel. Asian stock markets are a bit mixed with lower prices in Japan but small gains in China.
China, Russia and Iran participated in a summit of BRICS 
countries and other developing countries organized by Modi in New Delhi. The meeting agreed on a document that criticized the war in the Middle East and the use of sanctions and tariffs.
Following the US inflation data, we are changing our forecast and now expect 
the Fed to raise interest rates by 25 basis points on Wednesday. Core inflation was 0.3 per cent m/m and 2.4 per cent y/y, compared with consensus of 0.2 and 2.4 per cent, respectively. Although the deviation is small, our and the market's interpretation is that a majority of the Fed believes that the decline in inflation is going too slowly. The market is pricing in about an 85% probability of a hike on Wednesday, another hike later this year and another in 2027. Analysts in Bloomberg's consensus are slightly more divided, but nearly 50 percent expect a hike on Wednesday. However, a relatively large portion of the responses in the survey were provided before the August CPI. U.S. long-term interest rates fell back slightly initially but then rose and closed at the highest level since 2006. What the high long-term interest rates mean for the degree of monetary policy tightening is unclear, but neither the Fed nor the ECB seem to be paying much attention to this at present. More about the CPI and the Fed 
here.
The ECB raised interest rates and reiterated that inflation risks are mainly on the upside. 
 Expectations of further interest rate hikes rose and the market is now pricing in a 76 percent probability of a hike in October and a significant probability of another hike in December. Incoming data will guide policy going forward, but the question is what it means when the ECB raises interest rates even though there are still no clear signs of either indirect inflationary effects or second-round effects via wages. At the same time, growth risks are on the downside, and it is not difficult to imagine how French voters might react to higher energy prices and interest rates ahead of the presidential election in April next year. Since the beginning of July, the yield on the ten-year French government bond has risen by almost 90 basis points, while the interest rate differential with Germany has gradually widened. The French ten-year yield is now higher than the corresponding rate in both Greece and Italy. To contribute to pushing up already high interest rates in this situation seems to me to be less balanced.
Nordic key stories
Election night's preliminary distribution of seats, 175-174 in favor of the opposition, still stands,
 although the final election results will not be available until Wednesday. The opposition currently leads by 176-173, but the foreign votes are expected to shift the result slightly in favor of the government side. The assessment is that this will not be enough to change the the result to a government win. After that, complicated government negotiations with uncertain outcomes are likely to await. Magdalena Andersson has been pointed out as a possible candidate for prime minister, while Ulf Kristersson has opened the door to trying to remain as prime minister in another coalition. The Center Party opposes a government with the Left Party and at the same time needs to get both the Christian Democrats and the Liberals on board for the centrist solution the party advocates to be possible. So far, the market seems to be taking the election results in stride, even though the krona has weakened by barely one Öre against the euro.
The Riksbank's business survey on Wednesday 
will be an important piece of the puzzle ahead of next week's interest rate announcement, where companies' price plans are in focus. The low inflation in August supported our forecast that the Riksbank will wait until spring to raise interest rates, but the ECB's hawkish interest rate hike has changed the conditions. The market is now pricing in around one and a half hikes before the end of the year, and the question is to what extent the Riksbank can stick to the message from August that the Executive Board has time to wait before the interest rate needs to be raised.
After the rise in recent days, energy prices are higher 
than indicated by the futures market in June. However, the futures curves are still clearly pointing downwards, and market expectations for prices in twelve months' time have changed relatively little. The same applies to electricity prices. Growth is increasing, but as long as the weakness in the labour market does not reverse, the recovery is fragile, and a prolonged period of high energy prices increases the risk of a downturn in consumption in the autumn.
The combination of a hawkish ECB and signs of a weaker krona is putting pressure on the Riksbank.
 Nevertheless, our assessment is that the Executive Board is largely sticking to the strategy communicated in June and August. However, the ECB's hawkish announcement has increased uncertainty compared with our analysis ahead of the interest rate announcement published last week (read more 
here

articles.title: Svåra regeringsförhandlingar väntar efter jämnt val
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Trots högre räntor steg S&P 500 steg med nästan en procent i fredags 
och ligger mer än 10 procent högre än före Iran-kriget, även om index har fallit något från toppnivåerna i mitten av augusti. Börsterminerna pekar däremot nedåt under morgonen, drivet av ett högre oljepris efter att Saudiarabien stängt en oljeledning till följd av attacker. Ett möte mellan Iran och andra Gulfstater om hur Hormuzsundet ska kunna öppnas avslutades utan resultat på grund av oenighet. Brentoljan stiger med omkring tre dollar till 108 USD/fat. Asien börserna är lite blandade med lägre kurser i Japan men små uppgångar i Kina.
Kina, Ryssland och Iran deltog i ett toppmöte för BRICS-länderna 
och andra utvecklingsländer som arrangerades av Modi i New Delhi. Mötet enades om ett dokument som kritiserade kriget i Mellanöstern samt användningen av sanktioner och tullar.
Efter den amerikanska inflationsstatistiken ändrar vi vår prognos och räknar nu med 
att Fed höjer räntan med 25 punkter på onsdag. Kärninflationen blev 0,3 procent m/m och 2,4 procent y/y, jämfört med konsensus på 0,2 respektive 2,4 procent. Även om avvikelsen är liten är vår och marknadens tolkning att en majoritet i Fed anser att nedgången i inflationen går för långsamt. Marknaden prisar in ca 85% sannolikhet för en höjning på onsdag, ytterligare en höjning senare i år och ännu en under 2027. Analytikerna i Bloombergs konsensus är något mer splittrade, men nästan 50 procent räknar med en höjning på onsdag. En relativt stor del av svaren i enkäten lämnades dock före augusti-KPI. Amerikanska långräntor föll tillbaka något initialt men steg därefter och stängde på den högsta nivån sedan 2006. Vad de höga långräntorna betyder för graden av penningpolitisk åtstramning är oklart, men varken Fed eller ECB verkar i nuläget lägga särskilt stor vikt vid detta. Mer om KPI och Fed 
här.
ECB höjde räntan och upprepade att inflationsriskerna främst ligger på uppsidan. 
Förväntningarna på ytterligare räntehöjningar steg och marknaden prisar nu in 76 procents sannolikhet för en höjning i oktober samt en betydande sannolikhet för ytterligare en höjning i december. Inkommande data kommer att styra politiken framöver, men frågan är vad det innebär när ECB höjer räntan trots att det ännu saknas tydliga tecken på vare sig indirekta inflationseffekter eller andrahandseffekter via lönerna. Samtidigt ligger tillväxtriskerna på nedsidan, och det är inte svårt att föreställa sig hur franska väljare kan reagera på högre energipriser och räntor inför presidentvalet i april nästa år. På presskonferensen avfärdade Lagarde de rekordhöga långräntorna som ett globalt fenomen. Sedan början av juli har räntan på den tioåriga franska statsobligationen stigit med nästan 90 punkter, samtidigt som ränteskillnaden mot Tyskland gradvis har ökat. Den franska tioårsräntan är nu högre än motsvarande ränta i både Grekland och Italien. Att i det läget bidra till att pressa upp redan höga räntor framstår för mig som mindre välavvägt.
Sverige
Valnattens preliminära mandatfördelning, 175–174 till oppositionens fördel, står sig fortfarande,
 även om det definitiva valresultatet kommer först på onsdag. Oppositionen leder just nu med 176-173 men utlandsrösterna väntas kunna flytta resultatet något till regeringssidans fördel, men bedömningen från valnatten är att det inte räcker för att ändra mandatfördelningen. Därefter väntar sannolikt komplicerade regeringsförhandlingar med osäker utgång. Magdalena Andersson har pekats ut som möjlig statsministerkandidat, samtidigt som Ulf Kristersson har öppnat för att försöka sitta kvar som statsminister i en annan koalition. Centern motsätter sig en regering med Vänsterpariet och behöver samtidigt få med sig både Kristdemokraterna och Liberalerna för att den mittenlösning partiet förespråkar ska bli möjlig. Marknaden verkar hittills ta valresultatet med ro, även om kronan har försvagats med knappt ett öre mot euron.
Riksbankens företagsundersökning på onsdag 
blir en viktig pusselbit inför nästa veckas räntebesked, där framför allt företagens prisplaner står i fokus. Den låga inflationen i augusti gav stöd åt vår prognos om att Riksbanken väntar till våren med att höja räntan, men ECB:s hökaktiga räntehöjning har förändrat förutsättningarna. Marknaden prisar nu in omkring en och en halv höjning före årets slut, och frågan är i vilken utsträckning Riksbanken kan hålla fast vid budskapet från augusti om att direktionen har tid att avvakta innan räntan behöver höjas.
Efter de senaste dagarnas uppgång ligger energipriserna högre 
än vad terminsmarknaden indikerade i juni. Terminskurvorna pekar dock fortfarande tydligt nedåt, och marknadens förväntningar på priserna om tolv månader har förändrats relativt lite. Detsamma gäller elpriserna. Tillväxten ökar, men så länge svagheten på arbetsmarknaden inte vänder är återhämtningen bräcklig, och en längre period med höga energipriser ökar risken för ett bakslag i konsumtionen under hösten.
Kombinationen av en hökaktig ECB och tecken på en svagare krona sätter press på Riksbanken.
 Vår bedömning är ändå att direktionen i huvudsak håller fast vid den strategi som kommunicerades i juni och augusti. ECB:s hökaktiga besked har dock ökat osäkerheten jämfört med vår analys inför räntebeskedet som publicerades förra veckan (läs mer

articles.title: Higher than expected CPI tips the balance for a September Fed hike
articles.heading: US Economy
articles.fulltext:
August core CPI surprised on the upside for a 0.3% m/m increase, beating the consensus (0.2% m/m) and raising some question marks about the degree of improvement in the underlying inflation trend. Given the recent strong emphasis within the Fed on the monthly data, we shift our forecast and now expect a 25 bp hike in September. The details were not all bad, but the conclusion for the core PCE still points to another 0.3% m/m increase, though the upcoming revision of this data is an uncertain factor. 
Key points
Headline CPI 0.4%, 3.4%, in line with consensus
Core CPI 0.3%, 2.4%, above the consensus
Preliminary estimates points to a 0.3% m/m for core PCE
September revision is an uncertain factor for the PCE, however
A September rate hike is now the main scenario
Markets price nearly 90% probability for a hike
August CPI is a disappointment for the Fed
August CPI inflation was a disappointment for the Fed after a couple of benign summer months. The core ex energy and food CPI exceeded expectations at 0.3% m/m (consensus 0.2%), though on the lower side (0.29%). The y/y rate declined by 0.1%-point to 2.4%, as expected. Total CPI increased as expected 0.4%, 3.4% on the back of renewed increases in energy prices and marginally higher prices on food.
The details were not all bad. Volatile components like communication, lodging away from home, airline fares, education and used cars and trucks were behind the faster price increases, while medical care and motor vehicle insurance worked in the other direction. 
Slowdown in goods prices
Goods prices were marginally lower than we expected. Core goods prices slowed to 0.1% m/m (July 0.2%), even as vehicle prices increased faster (used cars 0.4% for the second consecutive month, new vehicles 0.3%, up from 0.1% in July). Prices on IT goods slowed to a mere 0.1% m/m. These prices have come into focus given upward pressures on imported IT equipment due to the AI expansion, but in August the category that is most affected, computer and accessories, actually fell by 2.2%. This index has inflated core PCE compared to core CPI by 0.2-0.3%-points because of a significantly larger weight. Changes to the methodology in the upcoming 30 September revision makes it harder to assess the impact on August PCE, however. 
Rising prices on tourist services
Prices on hotels and air tickets stand out and increased by 2.4% and 2.7% respectively. However, tourist services are volatile. Hotel prices fell in both June and July, which makes it hard to judge the underlying trend.
Slower rents increases
Rents slowed from July and were marginally lower than expected and also slightly below the historical trend. Market rents, as measured by Zillow have picked up recently from very low levels, which is a reason to be cautious about extending the favorable trend for rents. Services prices ex rents were high, however, after a weak reading in July.
Another too high monthly increase for core PCE but revisions are an uncertain factor
Our preliminary estimate for the August core PCE points to another too high 0.3% m/m, at least before the revised methodology that will be introduced later this month for IT and legal and financial services. Current expectations are that the revisions may lower the PCE by a couple of tenths of percentage points but this would still mean an elevated, around 3% core PCE y/y.
Not good enough even for Fed doves
Fed Chair Warsh committed strongly to the Fed doing what it takes to get inflation back to target in his Jackson Hole speech. Several other Fed members said they were willing to wait for more proof of improvement in the underlying inflation trends after a couple of better inflation readings during the summer. Still, also these members have warned that they are getting closer to a point when the Fed needs to act, while Warsh concluded that he did not see the summer data as a “meaningful” change in the underlying trend. 
Rate hike in September is now the main scenario
Market pricing for a September hike moved from almost 70 to nearly 90% after the data. This puts heavy pressure on the Fed to deliver a hike to bolster its inflation credibility. We are now changing our forecast for the 15-16 September meeting to a 25 bp hike to a range of 3.75-4.00%. Higher energy prices, back above USD 100/bl, is an upside risk going forward. Waiting until the next meeting at 27-28 could put the Fed in a difficult situation, given the proximity to the midterm elections on November 3. 
Warsh has been very clear that it is the responsibility of the Fed to make sure that inflation returns to target. He has been equally clear that the Fed should not signal its next step. This means that the Fed should now be data dependent and taking its decision on a meeting-by-meeting basis. Inflation data during the fall will be key for whether the Fed can stop at one hike to safeguard credibility. We continue to see scope for renewed disinflation once the temporary effects from tariffs, energy and, to some extent, AI on IT, pass. Whether the Fed will get enough evidence on this in the coming months is uncertain, however. Continued upward pressure on yields will work in the other direction, with markets now doing some of the job for the Fed. Markets are already pricing a succession of rate hikes until mid-year 2026 and the Fed must now hope that delivering a hike could calm market doubts of the Fed’s willingness to do what it takes.

articles.title: All eyes on Fed ahead of an uncertain rate decision
articles.heading: The Week Ahead
articles.fulltext:
The Fed’s interest rate decision will be this week’s main event. Uncertainty is unusually high, but we are revising our forecast and now expect a 25 bp rate hike at next week’s policy meeting. We will also get rate decisions from the Bank of England and the Bank of Japan. We expect the BoE to keep rates unchanged, while the BoJ is expected to hike its policy rate. Sunday’s Swedish election looks, according to latest polls, set to be a close race. We will follow up the results in a webcast on Monday morning (in Swedish), see below. 
US:
All eyes on the Fed. Following a higher-than-expected August core CPI we change our view to a 25 bp hike. Uncertainty is higher than usual, but we believe the Fed needs to deliver a hike to bolster its inflation credentials. We will also get August data for retail sales and industrial production and early manufacturing surveys for September, which will provide more evidence on the economic momentum in Q3.
Euro area:
Next to many interesting ECB speeches we will focus on the German PPI numbers and final inflation figures for August. In addition, the ECB wage tracker and inflation expectations will be important. On the political front, we will keep a close eye on the German state elections in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Berlin (both on September 20) as well as Ursula von der Leyen's speech about the State of the European Union (September 16).
Sweden:
Final CPI will reveal the drivers of the downside surprise in August. Household consumption, unemployment and the Riksbank’s business survey will give interesting clues about the economic recovery. The Swedish election results will gradually become clear during Monday morning. If the election is a very close call, we may have to wait until the middle of the week for the final result.
Norway:
Norges Bank’s upcoming September 24, rate decision will be a close call, and the Regional Network Report can provide some final insights. We will pay extra attention to 
inflation indicators, e.g., wage growth expectations, capacity constraints, labour shortages and employment expectations. Norges Bank regards a negative output gap as vital in order to bring inflation towards target.

articles.title: Worries about oil prices, bond yields and AI
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
Stock markets were gloomy yesterday, with the S&P 500 ending at -0.6% and the Nasdaq at -0.7%. Both oil prices and bond rate developments are worrying markets. Brent oil is trading just below $108/barrel this morning and long-term interest rates continued to rise yesterday. In the US, the 10-year yield was up 12 points and is now trading at 4.97%, the highest level since 2007. If we go even further back in time, we also note that today it is exactly 25 years since September 11, 2001. Probably the global event that has most etched itself in my memory in my and many others' professional lives.
Hawkish from the ECB. 
 As expected, the ECB raised interest rates by 25 basis points yesterday to 2.50%. The decision was unanimous and although it did not contain any guidance on what it intends to do next, it is a signal that the ECB revised up its inflation forecast for the next two years in light of higher energy prices. The development of energy prices will be decisive for whether the ECB will continue to hike. More about how we view the ECB 
here
. Our own Riksbank will not deliver its interest rate announcement until 24 September, and most likely rates will remain unchanged at 1.75%. Still, we believe that the Riksbank will use its rate path, to signal a 60 percent (15 basis point) probability of a hike in coming months. More on that 
here
. 
AI is worrying.
 Open AI CEO Sam Altman is reported to have suggested internally that the leading AI labs voluntarily slow down the development of new AI models. This week, there have been several warnings that AI is about to become dangerous. On Tuesday, an Open AI employee, who also previously worked at Anthropic, quit in protest and accused both companies of "gambling with our lives". Above all, it is the development of RSI (Recuring Self-Improvement), where new AI models improve themselves without human intervention, that raises concerns. There is no doubt that the technology is becoming "scary" powerful. Earlier this week, a swarm of AI agents from Open AI solved the so-called Navier Stokes equations that describe how liquids and gases flow. Human mathematicians have been working unsuccessfully to find a solution to this problem for 90 years. The AI agents did it in 88 hours...
In Asia, the stock markets are down today. 
Japan stands at -2.2%, Hong Kong at -0.9% and South Korea at -2.0%. Ahead of the opening here at home, US stock market futures are pointing slightly up, while European stock market futures are close to zero. There have only been small movements in the foreign exchange market during the night. 
US inflation in focus. 
 We have no Swedish or European data today and the statistics agenda is dominated by the US CPI figure for August. On the importance scale, it is unchallenged number one among US macro data and the expectation is that core inflation will fall back a tenth to 2.4% y/y. 
Nordic key stories
Swedish nail-biter on Sunday. 
 With two days left until the Swedish election, the opposition still looks to have a slight lead, but there is no doubt that the election wind has turned in favor of the Tidö parties lately. The latest poll gives the opposition a lead of 2.6 percentage points, but that difference is within the statistical margin of error. If you remember election night 2022, both TV4's and SVT's exit polls pointed to victory for the left, but then things slowly swung during the night in favor of the Tidö parties and the election was not completely decided until all votes had been counted on Wednesday.
Have a great Friday

Går vi ännu längre tillbaka i tiden noterar vi självklart också att det idag är exakt är 25 år sedan 11:e september 2001. Antagligen den globala händelse som allra mest etsat sig fast i minnet i mitt och många andras yrkesliv.
Hökigt från ECB. 
ECB höjde som väntat räntan med 25 punkter igår till 2,50%. Beslutet var enhälligt och även om det inte innehöll någon guidning om vad man tänker göra härnäst så är det en signal att ECB mot bakgrund av högre energipriser reviderade upp inflationsprognosen för de kommande två åren. Utvecklingen för energipriserna blir avgörande för om ECB kommer fortsätta höja. Mer om hur vi ser på ECB 
här
. Vår egen Riksbank kommer med sitt räntebesked först den 24 september och där talar det mesta för att räntan ligger still på 1,75%. Däremot tror vi att Rix med räntebanan väljer att signalera 60 procents (15 punkters) sannolikhet för en höjning framöver. Mer om det 
här

Att tekniken håller på att bli ”läskigt” kraftfull råder det ingen tvekan om. Tidigare i veckan löste en svärm av AI-agenter från Open AI, de så kallade Navier Stokes, ekvationerna som beskriver hur vätskor och gaser flödar. Mänskliga matematiker har utan framgång jobbat med att hitta en lösning på det problemet i 90-år. AI-agenterna gjorde det på 88 timmar…
I Asien är det nedåt på börserna idag. 
Japan står på -2,2%, Hongkong på -0,9% och Sydkorea på -2,0%. Inför öppningen här hemma pekar amerikanska börsterminer lite upp medan de europeiska ligger nära nollan. Det har bara varit små rörelser på valutamarknaden under natten. 
Amerikansk inflation i fokus.

articles.title: Hur du undviker att förlora alla dina pengar
articles.heading: Veckans tanke
articles.fulltext:
Du kan ha rätt om marknaden, rätt om bolaget och rätt om tekniken och ändå på något sätt lyckas med att bli ruinerad. Att vara framgångsrik på lång sikt i sina investeringar handlar faktiskt mycket om att inte först förlora allt på vägen dit. I den här Veckans Tanke går jag igenom några enkla men viktiga samband kring hur det hänger ihop och ett par varnande exempel på hur det kan gå fel.
Föreställ dig följande erbjudande: Du får kasta ett mynt. Om det blir krona ökar ditt kapital med 50 procent. Får du klave minskar det med 40 procent. Borde du acceptera spelet?
Är din strategi bara att maximera det förväntade utfallet är svaret ett obetingat "ja". Har du 1 000 000 kr är sannolikheten lika stor att du vinner 500 000 kr som att du förlorar 400 000 kr. Det förväntade värdet för utfallet är alltså positivt med 50 000 eller 5 procent.
Många kanske spontant tänker att det ändå känns lite riskabelt att spela trots att man har oddset på sin sida men om man bara får möjlighet att spela många gånger i rad. Ja då borde ju vinsterna med tiden bli större än förlusterna eftersom man vid varje spel har en statistisk fördel.
Men om du faktiskt sätter dig ner och spelar det här spelet två gånger så är, hör och häpna, det mest troliga att du förlorar pengar. För att göra det lite enklare att förstå ser du nedan de möjliga utfallen över två kast (om du spelar med 1 kr i stället för en miljon). Lägg märke till att tre av fyra möjliga utfall lämnar dig med mindre än du började med. Genomsnittet dras upp av det enda riktigt bra utfallet så att snittet av de fyra möjliga utfallen hamnar på +10,25 procent.
Faktum är att efter att du spelat tillräckligt många gånger är det nästan säkert att du har förlorat merparten av dina pengar. Processen är icke-ergodisk. Det vill säga det inte är samma sak om 100 spelare spelar spelet EN gång var som att EN spelare spelar spelet 100 gånger i rad. Själva myntkastandet i sig är visserligen en ergodisk process (dvs det är ingen skillnad om en spelare kastar 100 gånger i rad jämfört med att 100 spelare kastar en gång var).
Men detsamma gäller inte kapitalet du satsar. Här spelar det stor roll hur länge du har hållit på och vad som hänt dessförinnan. Om det blir krona eller klave i kast 56 är helt oberoende av vad det blivit tidigare. Men hur mycket pengar du har kvar efter 56 kast beror väldigt mycket på hur de 55 föregående kasten gick. Eftersom varje nytt kast verkar multiplikativt på hela kapitalet behövs betydligt högre procentuella vinster för att kompensera för en viss procentuell förlust. 
Att kasta krona eller klave 100 gånger ger 2^100 unika sekvenser (krona, klave, klave, krona etc …) eller ungefär 1,27x10^30 stycken. Av alla dessa 1,27 kvintiljoner olika banor kommer den stora majoriteten eller drygt 86 procent att sluta med förlust efter 100 kast. Ökar man antalet kast till 1 000 stycken är sannolikheten att gå med förlust hela 99,99 procent. Fortfarande kommer dock ungefär 0,01 procent av banorna att ge plus och några banor kommer att ha givit enorma vinster.
Snittavkastningen är hela tiden +5 procent per kastomgång, vilket över 1 000 kast ger ett genomsnittligt förväntat värde på över 1,5x10^21 gånger insatsen när man summerar utfallen över alla banor. Problemet för dig är att du inte kommer att få snittavkastningen utan det som blir resultatet av just din unika bana av 1000 kast, där statistiskt 99,99 procent av dem slutar på minus. 
I portföljsammanhang kallas detta ”volatility drag”. Det är den bromskloss på ränta-på-ränta-effekten som uppstår eftersom procentuella upp- och nedgångar i utvecklingen i en investeringsportfölj inte är symmetriska. Om ditt kapital minskar med 50 procent behöver det därefter växa med 100 procent för att du ska vara tillbaka där du startade. Ju större svängningarna är upp och ned ju större blir ditt ”volatility drag”. Det som fäller myntspelaren är att det geometriska medelvärdet i spelet är mindre än ett. Den förväntade vinsten är inte tillräckligt stor för att kompensera för den höga volatiliteten och det gör tiden till din fiende. 
För att tiden i stället ska arbeta för dig måste du ha en portfölj där den förväntade avkastningen har ett geometriskt medelvärde som är högre än ett. I myntexemplet hade vinstkasten behövt ge dig 68 procent i vinst för att du ska gå plus över tiden.
Förr eller senare går det åt skogen
Så vad kan vi ta med oss av detta när det gäller investeringar? Jo att förr eller senare så kommer något dåligt att hända och ju längre du håller på och investerar desto större är sannolikheten att det händer just dig. Har du en portfölj som bara består av en eller några få aktier som rör sig rätt mycket upp och ned så är att vara långsiktig faktiskt inget framgångsrecept.
Några kanske har läst om en amerikansk studie som publicerades tidigare i år. I studien (
här
) har forskaren Hendrik Bessembinder gått igenom avkastningen för nästan 30 000 amerikanska börsföretag under de senaste 100 åren. I studien visar han att bara drygt 1000 av företagen tillsammans stod för hela börsens överavkastning (dvs avkastningen som översteg korta ränteplaceringar). Hade du bara slumpmässigt valt en aktie och haft den under hela sin noterade livstid hade du sannolikt förlorat pengar då medianavkastningen för alla aktier var -6,9 procent. Risken är stor att företaget du investerat i förr eller senare drabbas av en allvarlig kris. Då är det betydligt bättre att köpa en fond som investerar brett. Då är du säker på att få med de få vinnarna även om det sker till priset av att du också investerar i ett antal företag som går i konkurs.
Håll dig borta från belåning
En annan sak som kan skada dig rejält är att belåna portföljen för att på så sätt få en hävstång på avkastningen. Din förväntade avkastning går visserligen upp med antalet gånger du belånat portföljen (om man bortser från räntekostnaden för lånet) men det gör också variansen i avkastningen som är det som avgör storleken på portföljens ”volatility drag”.
Problemet är att medan den förväntade avkastningen ökar linjärt med belåningen så ökar variansen med kvadraten av hävstången. Har du en belåning på 100 procent så dubblas din förväntade avkastning, dvs. hävstången är 2, men variansen i portföljen ökar med 4 gånger.
Just detta drabbade nyligen en av de mest hypade AI-fonderna i världen. Den 24-årige Leopold Aschenbrenners AI-fond Situational Awareness hade en belåningsgrad på upp till 4 gånger, vilket drabbade fonden hårt under den minikrasch som AI-aktier hade i somras. ”Margin calls” tvingade fram försäljningar i hast som resulterade i gigantiska förluster. Fondens kapital föll från 45 till omkring 10 miljarder dollar under en enda månad. Professionella investerare brukar bara använda belåning som ett sätt att öka avkastningen om risken (volatiliteten) i portföljen är så låg så att volatilitetsdraget kan hållas nere.
Håll avkastningen uppe och volatiliteten nere
Nyckeln till att nå positiv avkastning över tid är att samtidigt som man strävar efter en hög förväntad avkastning måste man också hålla nere volatiliteten, eftersom den annars äter upp ränta-på-ränta-effekten. I grunden handlar allt detta om att tillväxten i en portfölj över tid bestäms av det geometriska medelvärdet inte det aritmetiska, som vi oftast använder i andra sammanhang. Det geometriska medelvärdet är känsligt för hög volatilitet i avkastningen. Nu är det ju tyvärr så att ju högre förväntad avkastning man siktar på desto mer riskfylld och volatil blir också placeringen. Så finns det något sätt att hitta en bra balans mellan dessa två?
Att gå ”full Kelly”
Här kliver Kellykriteriet in på scenen. Formeln utvecklades 1956 av Bell Labs-forskaren John L. Kelly. Han ville publicera den under titeln "Information Theory and Gambling", men AT&T stoppade det av rädsla för att associeras med illegal vadhållning så titeln fick ändras till ”A New Interpretation of Information Rate”. Det dröjde dock inte länge förrän både hasardspelare och kvantitativa investerare insåg att formeln också kunde användas för att matematiskt fastställa den positionsstorlek som maximerar kapitalets geometriska tillväxt över tid, utan att för den skull innebära att man riskerar att bli ruinerad.
f: optimal andel av kapitalet att satsa, b: vinstodds (1 = en satsad krona ger en krona i vinst), p: sannolikheten för vinst, q: sannolikheten för förlust, alltså 1-p
Föreställ dig en investering där du bedömer att du har 60 procents chans att dubbla dina pengar (alltså vinstodds = 1) men att det samtidigt är 40 procents risk att företaget går i konkurs och du förlorar allt. Applicerar vi Kelly-kriteriet får vi resultatet att du ska satsa precis 20 procent av ditt kapital för att optimera utfallet så att du inte ger bort för mycket avkastning i onödan, men att du samtidigt inte riskerar att förlora för mycket av ditt kapital. 
Att i exemplet ovan satsa en femtedel av kapitalet kallas på traderjargong att ”go full Kelly”. Det ses dock av de flesta erfarna investerare som rätt riskabelt och oansvarigt eftersom verkligheten nästan aldrig är så tillrättalagd som i exemplet ovan. I praktiken är det väldigt svårt att korrekt uppskatta sannolikheterna för olika scenarion samtidigt som de flesta investerare också tenderar att överskatta sin egen ”förmåga” med risk för att man snabbt hamnar i ett läge av överallokering där volatilitetsdraget blir för stort. Därför tillämpar luttrade investerare oftast ”half Kelly”. Genom att halvera den teoretiskt optimala positionen behåller man omkring 75 procent av den optimala tillväxttakten samtidigt som volatiliteten halveras och risken för stora drawdowns minskar dramatiskt.
Sensmoralen ur ett ergodicitetsperspektiv är enkel: Lägg aldrig alla ägg i samma korg och var mycket försiktig med att belåna din portfölj! Tänk på att de flesta överskattar sin egen förmåga att hitta vinnare och att vara långsiktig faktiskt inte är någon garanti för ett bra utfall över tiden om du har för volatila tillgångar i portföljen. Överlever du inte de statistiska svackorna längs vägen spelar det ingen roll om du får rätt till slut. Konsten att vinna i längden handlar framför allt om konsten att inte först förlora allt på vägen dit.

articles.title: ECB hikes interest rates to combat higher energy prices
articles.heading: ECB Review
articles.fulltext:
As expected, the ECB today raised its three key interest rates by 25 bp, bringing the deposit rate to 2.50%. The decision to hike was unanimous, with no commitment to future action. Inflation was revised upwards for 2027-2028, while growth is seen as more resilient. No spillovers from higher energy prices are evident, but they are key for the ECB inflation profile from the end of 2026.
Key points
25 bp rate hike
Still data-dependent and following a meeting-by-meeting approach
Inflation revised upwards for 2027-2028, reflecting more persistent effects from higher energy prices
Key conclusions from the Q&A at the press conference
The decision to raise rates by 25 bp was unanimous
No view on the direction of the next move and no debate on the future rate path
The ECB was surprised by the resilience of the economy, but also by lower-than-expected inflation
The ECB now sees energy pressures keeping inflation above target for an “extended period”
Forecast revisions and alternative scenarios
Compared with June, the baseline projections for both headline and core inflation are unchanged for 2026. However, inflation projections, for both headline and core inflation, have been revised upwards for 2027 and 2028. This likely reflects the greater persistence of the energy-price shock. We also note that the overshoot in 2028 is quite small, but nevertheless symbolic. The baseline projection for GDP growth has been revised upwards for 2026-2027, reflecting the greater-than-expected resilience of the economy. Overall, the new projections can be interpreted as hawkish.

Regarding the inflation forecast, the upward revisions are due to higher energy prices. The upward adjustment to the core inflation forecast is not surprising, given that oil and natural gas prices point to an outcome close to the adverse scenario from June. Indeed, the 2027 core inflation forecast lies between the June baseline and the June adverse scenario.
To illustrate the uncertainty surrounding the conflict in the Middle East, the baseline projections are complemented by updated alternative scenarios: a mild, an adverse and a severe scenario. These scenarios differ in terms of the strength of indirect and second-round effects on inflation. Both the adverse and severe scenarios show inflation, both headline and core, remaining above target throughout the forecast period.
No spillovers yet, but key going forward
The ECB acknowledges that no spillovers from high energy prices to broader inflation have been visible so far but believes they will emerge at a later stage. Indeed, a key reason behind the ECB raising its inflation profile already in March/June was the expected spillovers from energy, taking into account the experience from 2021-2024 (i.e. a stronger pass-through 
than historical relationships in standard models would suggest). 
As we read the ECB staff projections, these effects will start to kick in from Q4 2026 and peak in H1 2027. Hence, we will have to wait a few more months before the ECB’s inflation profile is truly put to the test. As President Lagarde pointed out, the longer energy prices remain elevated, the more likely spillovers become. Although services inflation remains a key driver, the higher inflation profile to a large extent also reflects higher core goods inflation.
Unless energy prices fall and the situation in the Middle East improves, it is difficult to see the ECB staff making major changes to their projections in the December forecasting round. In that case, the ECB will most likely continue 
hiking,

our 
current forecast. However, President Lagarde pointed out 
that 
conditions can change quickly, and we will monitor upcoming speeches to get a sense of the current balance within the Governing Council.
Market impact 
Despite policy rate expectations having increased sharply over the summer, today’s message from the ECB pushed expectations for the next 12 months around 15bp higher. Markets now fully discount three further rate hikes, with the deposit facility rate reaching 3.25% by summer 2027.
